pullRequests.title: M PLUS Rounded 1c: Version 1.060 (hotfix)
pullRequests.body:
@aaronbell 

Fixes #11250.

### The problem

The binaries served for M PLUS Rounded 1c are the original 2016 Rounded M+ files (added in bf19077 as `ofl/roundedmplus1c`, then copied unchanged to `ofl/mplusrounded1c` in #9332). There are no upstream sources, so they have never been rebuilt. Two naming issues break the family on desktop:

1. **Bold shows up as a separate family.** In the Windows name records of the Bold, nameID 1 is `Rounded Mplus 1c Bold` instead of `Rounded Mplus 1c`. Font menus show a family "Rounded Mplus 1c Bold" with a single style, and the main family has no 700 weight, so apps like Krita jump from Medium to ExtraBold when Bold is requested.
2. **Thin is listed as a second "Light".** The Thin has `usWeightClass` 250 (METADATA says 100). fontconfig maps this to a weight between ExtraLight and Light, so KDE and other Linux apps display two "Light" styles.

### The fix

This is a minimal hotfix. Only the `name`, `OS/2` and `head` tables change; outlines, hinting and OpenType layout are untouched.

- Bold: nameID 1 set to `Rounded Mplus 1c`, so Regular and Bold form the RIBBI family again.
- Thin: `usWeightClass` changed from 250 to 100.
- `fsSelection` REGULAR/BOLD bits and `macStyle` set consistently on all styles.
- Legacy Mac (platform 1) name records removed, as done for M PLUS 1p in #4981.
- Version bumped from 1.059 to 1.060 (`head.fontRevision`, nameID 3 and 5).

### What is intentionally not changed

The internal family name stays `Rounded Mplus 1c` (PostScript `RoundedMplus1c-*`), even though the API name is `M PLUS Rounded 1c`. As discussed with @aaronbell in #11250, this is a derivative of M+ with its own original name, onboarded before the M PLUS naming convention. Keeping that name avoids breaking existing desktop installs, and it leaves room for a future official rounded M PLUS family without overlapping names.

pullRequests.title: gemini-triage-font: pin actions and scope the app token
pullRequests.body:
Fixes the failing [GitHub Actions Scan](https://github.com/google/fonts/actions/runs/42206287350/job/127854718463) seen on #11254 and on #11253.

**Why it fails.** The scan only runs when a PR's workflow files differ from main. Any branch cut between #11131 and the latest triage change ships an older copy of `gemini-triage-font.yml`, so the scan runs and finds three mandatory `unpinned-uses` findings plus two high `github-app` findings. Those findings are also present on main, so every such PR goes red.

**Changes**
- Pin `actions/checkout`, `fonttools/setup-fontspector` and `google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli` to commit hashes, with ratchet comments.
- `persist-credentials: false` on the checkout. No later step pushes.
- Remove the app-token step from the `triage` job. Nothing in that job reads the minted token.
- Scope the `label` job's app token to `issues: write` and `organization-projects: write`, matching the apply and project-board steps.

`zizmor --offline` (1.30.1) reports no findings for the file.

Open PRs that already fail this scan, such as #11254, need a rebase or a merge from main after this lands.

pullRequests.title: Recursive: remove erroneous cyrillic-ext subset (#5825)
pullRequests.body:
## Summary
Closes #5825

This PR removes the erroneous `subsets: "cyrillic-ext"` declaration from `ofl/recursive/METADATA.pb`.

## Rationale
- The Recursive font family (by Arrow Type) is designed exclusively for Latin and Vietnamese scripts.
- Verified against the variable font binary `ofl/recursive/Recursive[CASL,CRSV,MONO,slnt,wght].ttf` using `fontTools`:
  - Exactly 0 characters exist in the Cyrillic Unicode blocks (`0x0400–0x052F`, `0x2DE0–0x2DFF`, `0xA640–0xA69F`).
- Having `cyrillic-ext` declared in `METADATA.pb` causes Recursive to falsely appear in search results when users filter by Cyrillic on fonts.google.com, leading to missing glyphs / fallback rendering.
- Follows the exact metadata subset cleanup pattern from PR #11183.

## Checks
- [x] Font binary character map contains zero Cyrillic characters.
- [x] Validated `.ci/whatchanged.py` categorizes this as `CheckType.MODIFIED_FAMILY_METADATA`.
- [x] Protobuf syntax and formatting validated.

pullRequests.title: Update test_font_tags.py
pullRequests.body:
In adding a bunch of new tag data to the `families.csv`, I realized that there are situations where a tag may be active at the default location (MONO@0), but be inactive at a different location (MONO@1). "Monospace/Monospace" is a great example which can be set to 100 at the default location but needs to be set to 0 at other instances on the variable axis. 

This PR implements a change to the test_font_tags file to allow this to occur. It is required for https://github.com/google/fonts/pull/10688 to move forward.
